headline: A Dog That Sniffs Out Sea Pests Wins Award

sentences.text: A dog in the UK has a very special job.
Her name is Sgiath.
She can smell a small sea animal called a sea squirt.
The sea squirt is a problem for boats and the sea.
People gave Sgiath a big prize this week.
A dog called Sgiath has won a prize as animal of the year in the UK.
She has a job that no other dog in the country has done before.
Sgiath was trained to smell a sea animal called a sea squirt.
Some people call it sea vomit because of the way it looks.
It is not from the UK, and it grows fast on boats and rocks.
Sgiath helps people find it early, before it spreads too far.
A dog with an unusual talent has been named animal of the year in the UK.
Sgiath is believed to be the country's first dog trained to hunt sea squirts.
The sea squirt is a small marine creature with a nickname that is hard to forget: sea vomit.
It is an invasive species, which means it comes from somewhere else and spreads quickly.
It can cover boat hulls, ropes and the seabed, and it is difficult for people to spot.
Sgiath uses her nose to find it early, so that teams can remove it before it takes over.
Her trainers say the award shows how useful a well-trained dog can be for nature.
A dog that has been trained to track down an invasive marine pest has been honored as animal of the year in the UK.
Sgiath is thought to be the first dog in the country taught to sniff out sea squirts, a creature better known by its unflattering nickname, sea vomit.
The species is not native to British waters, and once it arrives it spreads rapidly across boat hulls, mooring ropes and the seabed.
Because it is hard to detect by eye, outbreaks are often noticed only after the pest has become firmly established.
Sgiath's sense of smell allows her to identify the creature at an early stage, giving removal teams a much better chance of stopping it.
Her handlers say the recognition highlights how detection dogs can support conservation work far beyond their traditional roles.
Similar dogs are already used around the world to find rare plants, protected animals and other unwanted species.
For Sgiath, the reward is simpler: a successful search ends with her favorite toy.
A dog trained to sniff out an invasive marine pest has been crowned animal of the year in the UK, in recognition of a role no other dog in the country is known to have performed.
Sgiath specializes in locating sea squirts, a creature whose appearance has earned it the unappealing nickname of sea vomit.
The species is not native to British waters, yet once introduced it colonizes boat hulls, mooring lines and the seabed with remarkable speed.
Because the pest is inconspicuous to the human eye, infestations are frequently discovered only after they have taken a firm hold.
Sgiath's acute sense of smell lets her flag the creature while it is still scarce, giving removal teams a realistic chance of containing it.
Her handlers say the award underlines how detection dogs can contribute to conservation well beyond the search-and-rescue work for which they are best known.
Comparable programs elsewhere already deploy dogs to find endangered plants, protected wildlife and other unwelcome arrivals.
For Sgiath herself, the motivation is refreshingly uncomplicated: every successful find is rewarded with her favorite toy.
